name: Burden of setting up or learning the technology
definition: Effort, confusion or difficulty encountered while getting the technology working, including reliance on family or support staff to do it.
applies_when: The speaker describes setup, installation, instructions or learning the device as effortful, confusing, or as something someone else had to do for them
does_not_apply_when: The speaker describes only routine day-to-day use of a device that is already working

name: Uncertainty about who sees the data and what happens to it
definition: Concern, confusion or a stated wish to know who reviews the data, when it is reviewed, where it is stored, or who else can access it.
applies_when: The speaker raises not knowing who looks at their readings, when they are looked at, or where the data goes or is stored
does_not_apply_when: The speaker discusses the readings themselves without reference to who sees them or where they go

name: Financial cost falling on the participant
definition: Any out-of-pocket expense the participant bears because of the service, including consumables, transport or connectivity.
applies_when: The speaker mentions something they have to pay for themselves, or the affordability of it
does_not_apply_when: The speaker mentions costs borne entirely by the health service or employer

name: Trust placed in a human clinician rather than the technology
definition: Expressions of confidence in a named or generic clinician, or of a preference for human judgement over device output.
applies_when: The speaker compares a clinician favourably with the technology, or describes valuing contact with a clinician
does_not_apply_when: A clinician is mentioned only as the person who referred them, with no judgement expressed

name: Quality of helpdesk or technical support
definition: Experience of contacting support: waiting, competence of the person, whether the problem was resolved.
applies_when: The speaker describes contacting a helpline, helpdesk or support service and how that went
does_not_apply_when: The speaker describes contact with clinical staff about their health rather than about the technology

name: Increased sense of agency over one's own condition
definition: The technology giving the participant feedback that changes how they understand or act on their own condition.
applies_when: The speaker describes seeing their own data and it changing their behaviour, understanding or sense of ownership
does_not_apply_when: The speaker describes behaviour change driven entirely by instruction from a clinician

name: Loss of in-person contact with the care team
definition: Fewer face-to-face appointments as a consequence of remote monitoring, and how the participant feels about that.
applies_when: The speaker notes seeing clinical staff less often, or something being missed because contact is remote
does_not_apply_when: The speaker describes contact being unchanged, or discusses appointment availability generally
